extracted.intended_audience: developers and implementers of MathML renderers, editors, converters, and software that consumes or produces MathML (web developers, browser vendors, accessibility/tooling authors)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and normative requirements for implementing, authoring, parsing, validating, and deploying MathML 3.0 (presentation and content MathML) in XML/HTML host environments and associated toolchains.

rubrics_metrics.name: MathML Conformance
rubrics_metrics.description: MathML Conformance (section 2.3.1) — rules that specify what it means for MathML instances and MathML processors to conform to the specification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The document contains normative conformance requirements for MathML usage and for processors; implementers must follow the conformance section and related normative text. See also handling of errors and attributes for unspecified data for additional conformance behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of Errors
rubrics_metrics.description: Handling of Errors (section 2.3.2) — normative guidance on how MathML processors should detect and respond to malformed or invalid MathML.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies expected behaviors when encountering errors in MathML (e.g., error-markup, <merror>, and recovery strategies). Implementations should follow the handling rules to ensure robust processing and interoperability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attributes for unspecified data
rubrics_metrics.description: Attributes for unspecified data (section 2.3.3) — how implementations should treat attributes used to carry data not otherwise specified by the standard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines semantics and recommended handling for attributes intended to carry unspecified or implementation-specific data; implementers should document and preserve such attributes appropriately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation Markup correctness and semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: Presentation Markup (Chapter 3) — criteria for presentation-oriented markup: what presentation elements represent, required arguments, special behaviors, directionality, displaystyle/scriptlevel, linebreaking, and fine-tuning warnings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implementers and authors must follow element-level definitions (e.g., <mi>, <mn>, <mo>, <mrow>, <mfrac>, <msqrt>, <msup>, <mtable>, <mfenced>, <maction>, etc.), obey required arguments and special behaviors, handle directionality and linebreaking, and heed warnings about fine-tuning presentation for consistent rendering.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content MathML correctness and intent
rubrics_metrics.description: Content Markup (Chapter 4) — intent and structure of content MathML, including strict content MathML, content dictionaries, encoding expression structure (<cn>, <ci>, <csymbol>, <apply>, <bind>, <share>, etc.), and operator/constant encodings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implementations must follow the content markup semantics and structure, support or transform to/from strict content MathML where required, and use content dictionaries consistently to ensure unambiguous mathematical meaning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strict Content MathML and transformations
rubrics_metrics.description: The Strict Content MathML Transformation (section 4.6) — rules for transforming general content/presentation markup to strict Content MathML.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tools that produce or consume content MathML should implement the specified transformation semantics to obtain strict content representations when needed; the spec describes required behavior for that transformation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mixing markup languages and annotation framework
rubrics_metrics.description: Mixing Markup Languages (Chapter 5) — annotation framework and elements (<semantics>, <annotation>, <annotation-xml>), annotation keys, alternate representations, content equivalents, annotation references, and combining presentation and content markup (parallel markup).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implementations should support the annotation framework and parallel markup patterns to carry both presentation and semantic information and to enable interoperation between presentation and content representations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interactions with the Host Environment
rubrics_metrics.description: Interactions with the Host Environment (Chapter 6) — invoking MathML processors, recognizing MathML in XML and HTML, resource types, names of encodings, transferring MathML, mixing with other formats, linking, and MathML/graphical markup interaction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines how MathML must be embedded, recognized and handled by host environments (XML, XHTML, HTML5). Implementers must follow recommended behaviors for transfer, embedding, mixing MathML with HTML/XHTML/non-XML contexts, and linking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transferring MathML — recommended behaviors
rubrics_metrics.description: Transferring MathML (section 6.3) — basic transfer flavor names and contents and recommended behaviors when transferring MathML between systems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies transfer formats and recommended handling (e.g., serialization choices); implementers should adopt these recommendations to avoid interoperability problems and preserve semantics during transfer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Using CSS with MathML
rubrics_metrics.description: Using CSS with MathML (section 6.5) — interaction of style sheets with MathML, including order of processing attributes versus style sheets and how CSS applies to MathML elements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implementations should follow the specified order of attribute and stylesheet processing and document the interaction so authors can reliably style MathML content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characters, Entities and Fonts handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Characters, Entities and Fonts (Chapter 7) — rules for Unicode character data, entity declarations, special characters not in Unicode, mathematical alphanumeric symbols, non-marking characters, anomalous characters, keyboard characters, pseudo-scripts and combining characters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implementers must correctly map MathML character and entity usage to Unicode and font systems, handle special or non-Unicode math characters as specified, and consider keyboard and combining character issues for correct rendering and accessibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parsing and Validation Schemas
rubrics_metrics.description: Parsing MathML (Appendix A) — use of MathML as well-formed XML, RelaxNG schema for MathML3 (full MathML, presentation and content grammars), DTD and XML Schema usage, validation issues, and parsing in XHTML/HTML contexts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors and tool authors should validate MathML instances against the provided RelaxNG or other schemas where applicable, follow grammar rules for presentation and content MathML, and adhere to the parsing guidance for correct interpretation in XML and HTML host documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Media Types for MathML instances
rubrics_metrics.description: Media Types Registrations (Appendix B) — selection and registration of media types for generic, presentation, and content MathML instances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When serving or packaging MathML, use the registered media types and follow the recommendations in Appendix B to ensure correct content negotiation and handling by clients.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operator Dictionary usage
rubrics_metrics.description: Operator Dictionary (Appendix C) — non-normative operator dictionary format, indexing, notes on lspace and rspace attributes, and operator dictionary entries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implementations should consult the operator dictionary for spacing and operator semantics; appendix explains format and spacing notes to achieve consistent operator presentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Test Suite and Implementation Reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Test Suite and Implementation Report — the Working Group maintains a comprehensive Test Suite; developers are encouraged to submit results; Test Results are public and show at least two interoperable implementations for each essential test.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implementers should run and submit results to the public Test Suite and Implementation Report to demonstrate interoperability. The presence of at least two interoperable implementations per essential test is a stated expectation for the ecosystem.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support for bidirectional text and international/elementary notations
rubrics_metrics.description: Support for bidirectional layout, linebreaking, and elementary math notations (chapter 3 additions such as mstack, mlongdiv, RTL examples): MathML 3 adds support for bidirectional layout and elementary math notations used in many countries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Renderers should correctly handle RTL scripts, directionality, and the new elementary math constructs to support international mathematical notation and consistent linebreaking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deprecation and backwards-compatibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Deprecation and changes from previous versions — some elements and attributes are deprecated, chapters restructured, and appendices updated; see Appendix F (Changes) for detailed change log.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors and implementers migrating from previous MathML versions should consult the change log and deprecated-elements lists (e.g., Appendix F and 4.5 Deprecated Content Elements) and implement recommended migration or compatibility strategies.

rubrics_metrics.name: W3C Patent Policy and essential claim disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent disclosure requirements — produced under the W3C Patent Policy; individuals with knowledge of patents containing Essential Claim(s) must disclose per section 6 of the W3C Patent Policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implementers and contributors should be aware of the W3C patent policy, check the public patent disclosure list, and follow instructions for disclosing patents to avoid IP issues when implementing or deploying functionality covered by MathML.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document status and normative vs non-normative material
rubrics_metrics.description: Status of the Document — this specification is a W3C Recommendation and contains normative and non-normative material; non-normative explanatory material has been moved to companion documents (e.g., MathML Primer).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implementers should treat normative clauses as binding for conformance; use companion documents (primer, examples) for non-normative guidance and learning, but rely on the Recommendation for conformance requirements.
